subject: history

source.track: IGCSE · ages 14–16 · Core content (Option A or B) plus at least one Depth study

note: The Core content and Depth studies are structured around a series of key questions. Key questions define the over-arching issues; focus points identify the issues that build understanding; specified content states what must be studied. The atlas tracks Option A, Option B and all five Depth studies.

program.section: Core content — Option A: the nineteenth century, 1848–1914
program.title: Were the revolutions of 1848 important?
topics: Why had liberalism and nationalism grown in influence by 1848?
Why were there so many revolutions in 1848?
Did the revolutions have anything in common?
Why did most of the revolutions fail?
Did the revolutions change anything?

program.section: Core content — Option A: the nineteenth century, 1848–1914
program.title: How was Italy unified?
topics: Why was Italy not unified in 1848–49?
How important was Garibaldi's contribution to unifying Italy?
Did Cavour help or hinder the unification of Italy?
How important for other European countries were moves towards Italian unification?

program.section: Core content — Option A: the nineteenth century, 1848–1914
program.title: How was Germany unified?
topics: Why was Germany not unified in 1848–50?
How did Bismarck bring about Austria's defeat of 1866?
How did Bismarck bring about France's defeat of 1870?
How far was Bismarck responsible for the unification of Germany?

program.section: Core content — Option A: the nineteenth century, 1848–1914
program.title: Why was there a civil war in the United States and what were its results?
topics: How far did slavery cause the Civil War?
What was the significance of Lincoln's election as president?
Why was the North able to win the war?
Did the war change anything?

program.section: Core content — Option A: the nineteenth century, 1848–1914
program.title: Why, and with what effects, did nations gain and expand their overseas empires in the nineteenth century?
topics: What were the motives behind European and US imperialism?
How varied were the impacts of European imperialism on Africans?
Why, and with what effects, did Indians resist British rule?
Why, and with what effects, did the United States gain former Spanish colonies?

program.section: Core content — Option A: the nineteenth century, 1848–1914
program.title: What caused the First World War?
topics: Did the Alliance System and global diplomacy make war more likely or less likely?
How far did colonial problems create tensions between the Great Powers?
Why were problems in the Balkans so difficult for the Great Powers to solve?
How did the assassination of Franz Ferdinand lead to war?

program.section: Core content — Option B: international relations from 1919
program.title: Was the Treaty of Versailles fair?
topics: What were the motives and aims of the Big Three at Versailles?
Why did the victors not get everything they wanted?
What was the impact of the Treaty on Germany up to the end of 1923?
Could the Treaty be justified at the time?

program.section: Core content — Option B: international relations from 1919
program.title: To what extent was the League of Nations a success?
topics: How far did weaknesses in the League's organisation and membership make failure inevitable?
How successful were the League's attempts at peacekeeping in the 1920s?
How far did the Depression make the League's work harder?
Why did the League fail in the 1930s?

program.section: Core content — Option B: international relations from 1919
program.title: How far was Hitler's foreign policy to blame for the outbreak of war in Europe in 1939?
topics: What were the long-term consequences of the Treaty of Versailles?
What were the consequences of the failures of the League of Nations in the 1930s?
Was the policy of appeasement justified?
How important was the Nazi–Soviet Pact?
Why did Britain and France declare war on Germany in September 1939?

program.section: Core content — Option B: international relations from 1919
program.title: Who was to blame for the Cold War?
topics: Why did the US–Soviet alliance begin to break down in 1945?
How had the USSR gained control of Eastern Europe by 1948?
How did the United States react to Soviet expansionism?
What were the consequences of the Berlin Blockade?
Who was more to blame for starting the Cold War: the United States or the USSR?

program.section: Core content — Option B: international relations from 1919
program.title: How effectively did the United States contain the spread of communism?
topics: The United States and events in Korea, 1950–53
The United States and events in Cuba, 1959–62
American involvement in Vietnam, 1955–75

program.section: Core content — Option B: international relations from 1919
program.title: How secure was the USSR's control over Eastern Europe, 1948–c.1989?
topics: Why was there opposition to Soviet control in Hungary in 1956 and Czechoslovakia in 1968, and how did the USSR react?
How similar were events in Hungary in 1956 and in Czechoslovakia in 1968?
Why was the Berlin Wall built in 1961?
What was the significance of Solidarity in Poland for the decline of Soviet influence in Eastern Europe?
How far was Gorbachev personally responsible for the collapse of Soviet control over Eastern Europe?

program.title: Depth study A — The First World War, 1914–18
topics: Why was there stalemate on the Western Front?
To what extent was it a world war?
How important were other fronts?
Why did Germany agree to an armistice in 1918?

program.title: Depth study B — Germany, 1918–45
topics: Was the Weimar Republic doomed from the start?
Why was Hitler able to dominate Germany by 1934?
How effectively did the Nazis control Germany, 1933–45?
What was it like to live in Nazi Germany?

program.title: Depth study C — Russia, 1905–41
topics: Why did the Tsarist regime collapse in 1917?
How did the Bolsheviks gain and hold onto power?
How far was the USSR a changed country by 1941?
How far did Stalin create a totalitarian state?

program.title: Depth study D — The United States, 1919–41
topics: How far did the US economy boom in the 1920s?
How far did US society change in the 1920s?
Why did the US economy collapse in 1929?
How successful was the New Deal?

program.title: Depth study E — The Second World War in Europe and the Asia–Pacific, 1939–c.1945
topics: How far was German military strength responsible for Hitler's victories, 1939–41?
Why did the Axis powers lose the war in Europe?
Why did Japan attack the United States?
Why were the atomic bombs dropped on Japan?
